title: Quest.cs
summary: The win/lose condition for an episode: collectible/stress/NPC criteria, an optional countdown timer, and the UnityEvents + scene-unlock logic that fire on success or failure.

notes.text: Groups this component under 'Mindscape/Quest' in the Add Component search instead of the root list.
Stable identifier for save data / cross-referencing — separate from the display name so renaming the quest doesn't break anything referencing it by id.
What shows in the Journal UI.
Whether this quest starts already active (most do) or needs to be turned on later via ActivateQuest().
The list of QuestCollectibleRequirement rows described above.

notes.match: [Tooltip("NPC names the player must finish talking to. Names are matched without case sensitivity.")]
notes.text: Plain strings, not NPC references — matched by name so quests don't need a hard scene reference to specific NPC GameObjects.
Cached so IsStressAccepted doesn't call FindAnyObjectByType every frame.

notes.match: public float EpisodeDuration => Mathf.Max(0f, episodeDurationMinutes * 60f + episodeDurationSeconds);
notes.text: EpisodeDuration is computed from minutes+seconds every time rather than cached, since either field could change in the Inspector during Play mode.
Time.timeScale = 0 freezes gameplay while the completion modal is up — Quest.Update uses unscaledDeltaTime specifically so its own timer logic still works if ever needed after this point.
One row of the 'Required Collectibles' list: either drag a specific CollectibleItem, or type a raw id string — RequiredId prefers the linked item's own itemId if one is assigned.

A tiny static pub/sub event completely decoupled from any specific Quest instance — any NPC conversation finishing anywhere raises this once, and every currently-enabled Quest's OnEnable subscription picks it up.
Optional stress-range requirement — both bounds default such that it's effectively disabled until requireStressRange is checked.
Timer fields split into minutes+seconds for a friendlier Inspector; both 0 disables the timer entirely (see EpisodeDuration below).
Designer-hookable UnityEvents for anything beyond the automatic unlock-next-chapter behavior — e.g. play a sound, trigger an animation.

Runtime state that needs to survive between Inspector refreshes but shouldn't be hand-edited, hence HideInInspector while still [SerializeField] (so it round-trips through play mode / prefab changes).
Small public read-only surface QuestHUDController and the custom Inspector query to display status.
Formats the countdown as MM:SS for the Journal HUD.
A quest with truly nothing configured (no collectibles, no stress range, no NPCs) is considered to have 'no criteria' — see EvaluateNow, which refuses to auto-complete such a quest.
Caches PlayerControls, sets the initial active/inactive state from activeOnStart, and starts the countdown fresh.
Subscribes to/unsubscribes from the static NPCConversationCompleted event only while this component is enabled — a standard pattern to avoid leaking subscriptions on disabled/destroyed objects.

Every frame while active and not yet completed: re-check criteria, and separately tick the countdown (using unscaled time so it isn't affected by a paused game-over screen elsewhere) and fail the episode if it hits zero.
Public API for designers to turn a quest on via a UnityEvent elsewhere (e.g. a trigger volume) — resets the timer unless the episode already ended.
Turns a quest off without resetting its progress.
Full reset back to a fresh, replayable state — used when retrying a failed episode.

The actual evaluation: bails early if inactive/already completed/has no criteria, checks all three criteria types, and on success persists the chapter unlock, fires the UnityEvent, freezes the game, and shows the completion screen.
Resets the countdown to the full configured duration.
Mirror image of success: marks the episode ended (but not completed), fires the failure UnityEvent, freezes time, and shows the game-over screen.
True automatically if there are no collectible requirements at all; otherwise every requirement must be satisfied by the shared BagUIController instance.
True automatically if the stress-range requirement isn't enabled; otherwise checks the player's current stress against the (auto-sorted) min/max bounds.
True only if every non-blank required NPC name has a case-insensitive match in talkedToNPCNames.
Used by the Journal UI to show 'x / y' progress per collectible requirement.
Used both internally (AreNPCsComplete) and by the Journal UI to show a per-NPC checkmark.

The NPCConversationCompleted event handler: records the name (once) and immediately re-evaluates, so a quest can complete the instant the last required NPC talk finishes rather than waiting for the next Update.
Any QuestMinigame fits here now — the breathing exercise, the Worry Courtroom, or your own.
The episode clock waits while a minigame is open, so a few minutes in the courtroom don't eat the timer.
The player left before finishing. Resetting 'triggered' lets the same trigger open it again.
Talking to an NPC again still re-checks their minigame trigger, so a minigame closed early can be reopened this way.
